name: Arron Banks

summary.text: Arron Banks is a British businessman and the principal funder of the Leave.EU campaign in the 2016 EU referendum. On 1 November 2018 the Electoral Commission announced that it had referred Banks, Better for the Country Ltd, Leave.EU and Elizabeth Bilney to the National Crime Agency, stating it had reasonable grounds to suspect that Banks was not the true source of £8 million in loans. On 24 September 2019 the NCA said it had found no evidence of criminal offences by Banks or Bilney and no evidence that a third party funded the loans. Banks called the allegations ludicrous and later brought a defamation complaint over the referral announcement, which was settled.

facts.claim: The Electoral Commission opened an investigation into payments to Better for the Country Ltd and Leave.EU in November 2017 and, on 1 November 2018, announced it had referred Banks, Better for the Country, Leave.EU and Elizabeth Bilney to the National Crime Agency, saying it had reasonable grounds to suspect Banks was not the true source of £8 million in loans and that an impermissible company, Rock Holdings Ltd of the Isle of Man, was involved.
facts.quote: reasonable grounds to suspect that Mr Banks was not the true source of the £8m loans

sources.title: Investigation into payments made to Better for the Country and Leave.EU
Insurance mogul and Leave campaigner referred to National Crime Agency
Public statement on NCA investigation into suspected EU referendum offences

facts.claim: The NCA's public statement of 24 September 2019 said it accepted the Electoral Commission's referral on 17 October 2018, covering potential offences under PPERA 2000 and company law, and that it had interviewed Banks and Bilney.
facts.quote: suspected electoral law offences covered by that referral, as well as any associated offences

sources.title: Public statement on NCA investigation into suspected EU referendum offences

facts.claim: The NCA concluded on 24 September 2019 that it had found no evidence that any criminal offences had been committed under PPERA or company law by Banks, Bilney, Better for the Country or Leave.EU, and no evidence that a third party funded the £8 million loans or that Banks acted as an agent for anyone; it would take no further action.

sources.title: Public statement on NCA investigation into suspected EU referendum offences
NCA says no evidence Leave.EU and Arron Banks broke law

facts.claim: Banks said when referred that he was confident a full investigation would end what he called ludicrous allegations, that there was no evidence of wrongdoing from the companies he owned, and that the referral was made under political pressure.
facts.quote: confident that a full and frank investigation will finally put an end to the ludicrous allegations

sources.title: Insurance mogul and Leave campaigner referred to National Crime Agency

facts.claim: Banks and Bilney brought a defamation complaint against the Electoral Commission and its director Bob Posner over the referral announcement; the parties reached a settlement in which the Commission accepted the NCA's conclusions while saying it still believed the referral was justified.

facts.claim: The Electoral Commission found in May 2018 that Leave.EU did not correctly report three regulated transactions from Banks totalling £6 million, as part of the breaches for which Leave.EU was fined £70,000.
facts.quote: three regulated transactions from Mr Arron Banks, totalling £6 million

facts.claim: The ICO's November 2018 report said it was investigating allegations that Eldon Insurance Services Limited shared customer data with Leave.EU; Banks said no customer data was used and that nobody had provided evidence to the contrary.
facts.quote: We are investigating allegations that Eldon Insurance Services Limited shared customer data obtained for insurance purposes with Leave.EU.

openQuestions: Was Banks's NCA investigation confined to the referred loans, or did any other investigation into his business dealings follow? The NCA statement did not rule out other matters.
The terms of the defamation settlement with the Electoral Commission are described only in general terms in the joint announcement.
